paper_metadata.title: Clinical and EEG Analysis of Patients With Idiopathic Generalized Epilepsy and Photosensitivity

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses a consecutive sample from a specialized epilepsy clinic, which is well-described. However, as a retrospective database study, there is no information on the total number of eligible patients versus those included, making it difficult to assess participation bias.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: epilepsy outpatient clinic database of the Department of Neurology (Istanbul Medical Faculty, Istanbul University).
items.reasoning: The source is a specific tertiary care epilepsy clinic, and the target population (IGE with photosensitivity) is clearly defined.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: Fifty consecutive patients with a diagnosis of IGE and having EEG or clinical evidence for photosensitivity have been identified from the epilepsy outpatient clinic database
items.reasoning: While 'consecutive' recruitment is mentioned, the specific timeframe for the database search and the total number of patients screened are not provided.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: The text mentions the last follow-up was in 2007, but does not specify the start or end dates of the recruitment period.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: Department of Neurology (Istanbul Medical Faculty, Istanbul University).
items.reasoning: The specific hospital and department are clearly identified.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: Inclusion criteria: Patients with a diagnosis of IGE and having EEG or clinical evidence for PS, follow-up period ≥ 1 year (last follow-up in 2007), no evidence of neurologic deficit or mental retardation, CT/MR scans normal or nonspecific/unrelated to epilepsy if performed.
items.reasoning: The criteria are explicit regarding diagnosis, follow-up duration, and exclusion of secondary epilepsies.

items.label: Adequate study participation

items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: The paper does not report how many patients met the criteria but were excluded due to missing records or refusal, so the participation rate is unknown.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Thirty-six female and 14 male patients with median age 25.5 (14-63) were included to the study... Table 1: Patient characteristics and seizure triggers
items.reasoning: Table 1 provides comprehensive baseline data including age, sex, age at onset, and family history.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study requires a minimum 1-year follow-up, but as a retrospective review, it does not account for patients who were lost to follow-up before that 1-year mark, potentially biasing the outcome toward those with better clinic adherence.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factors (seizure types and EEG characteristics) are well-defined and measured using standardized protocols (Waltz classification) and clinical records.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: The IPS response is graded according to Waltz's classification(22) by the investigators.
items.reasoning: The study uses a validated classification system for the primary prognostic factor (PPR).

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: EEG evidence for photosensitivity was obtained from available EEG traces... IPS protocol: The standard IPS protocol starts with eyes open for 5 seconds and then eyes closed for 5 seconds
items.reasoning: The use of a standard IPS protocol and review of actual EEG traces (not just reports) increases reliability.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: IPS-sensitivity range (Hz) 1-10, 10-20, 20-30, >30
items.reasoning: The frequency ranges used are standard in the literature and not derived post-hoc from the data.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: The standard IPS protocol starts with eyes open for 5 seconds and then eyes closed for 5 seconds; the stimulus trains of 5-10-15-20-25-30-35 Hz are given at a distance of 30 cm in a normally illuminated room.
items.reasoning: A uniform protocol was applied to all patients.

items.label: Proportion of data on PF available for analysis
items.prompt: Adequate proportion of the study sample has complete data for PF variable.
items.evidence_snippet: Fifty patients... identified from the epilepsy outpatient clinic database... EEG data: The following information was obtained from the available EEG reports/traces
items.reasoning: The study only included patients where these records were available.

items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: Imputation was not used; the study relied on available retrospective data.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (seizure freedom) is based on retrospective medical records, which rely on patient recall and clinician documentation, introducing potential measurement bias compared to prospective diaries.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Remission was defined as seizure free for ≥ 5 years, regardless of AED treatment status.
items.reasoning: The primary outcome (remission) is clearly defined with a temporal threshold.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: Clinical data: The following clinical parameters were assessed from the outpatient medical records
items.reasoning: Medical records are standard but subject to recall bias and inconsistent reporting by patients during clinic visits.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Clinical data: The following clinical parameters were assessed from the outpatient medical records
items.reasoning: All outcomes were derived from the same clinical database and record-keeping system.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study does not use multivariable analysis to adjust for potential confounders. While it identifies 'Absence Seizures' as a prognostic factor, it does not control for age of onset, treatment type, or syndrome (JME vs AE) in a single model.

items.label: Important Confounders Measured
items.prompt: All important confounders, including treatments (key variables in conceptual model: LIST), are measured.
items.evidence_snippet: diagnosis/syndrome (JME, AE or other IGE), sex, current age, age at onset of epilepsy, follow-up period... therapy (AED)
items.reasoning: The study measured the most relevant clinical confounders.

items.label: Definition of the confounding factor
items.prompt: Clear definitions of the important confounders measured are provided (e.g., including dose, level, and duration of exposures).
items.evidence_snippet: Valproic acid (VPA) constituted the AED therapy in the majority of the (62%) patients.
items.reasoning: While AED types are mentioned, specific doses or durations of specific treatments are not detailed.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Confounders
items.prompt: Measurement of all important confounders is adequately valid and reliable (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: assessed from the outpatient medical records
items.reasoning: Reliability is limited by the retrospective nature of the record review.

items.label: Method and Setting of Confounding Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of confounding measurement are the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: identified from the epilepsy outpatient clinic database
items.reasoning: All data came from the same clinical setting.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods are used if imputation is used for missing confounder data.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: No imputation was performed.

items.label: Appropriate Accounting for Confounding
items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the study design (e.g., matching for key variables, stratification, or initial assembly of comparable groups).
items.evidence_snippet: The cohort could be divided into three groups, depending on the type of syndrome: JME, AE and other IGE.
items.reasoning: The study uses stratification (subgroup analysis) but not matching or comparable group assembly at the design stage.

items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the analysis (i.e., appropriate adjustment).
items.evidence_snippet: For continuous variables, associations were evaluated using the Mann-Whitney U test... categorical variables were assessed by using the Chi-square
items.reasoning: The study only performed univariable analyses (Mann-Whitney, Chi-square). No multivariable regression was used to adjust for confounding.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The analysis is limited to univariable tests, which is insufficient for a prognosis study. However, the reporting of the results is transparent, and the limitations are acknowledged.

items.label: Presentation of analytical strategy
items.prompt: There is sufficient presentation of data to assess the adequacy of the analysis.
items.evidence_snippet: The statistical analysis was done with SPSS for Windows version 15.0... Statistical significance was set at p<0.05.
items.reasoning: The tests used are clearly stated.

items.label: Model development strategy
items.prompt: The strategy for model building (i.e., inclusion of variables in the statistical model) is appropriate and is based on a conceptual framework or model.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: There was no multivariable model building strategy.

items.prompt: The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study.
items.evidence_snippet: Mann-Whitney U test... Chi-square (Pearson Chi-square) test.
items.reasoning: While these tests are correct for simple comparisons, they are inadequate for determining independent prognostic factors in a cohort.

items.label: Reporting of results
items.prompt: There is no selective reporting of results.
items.reasoning: The authors report both significant and non-significant findings across multiple clinical and EEG variables.
